subject: general
question: In July 2021, which government's Women and Child Development (WCD) department implemented a policy to identify destitute children, and assigned the responsibility of identifying and rehabilitating them to 10 of its agencies?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Delhi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Delhi government’s Women and Child Development (WCD) department implemented a policy in July 2021 to identify and rehabilitate destitute children.
 
• The policy assigns the responsibility of identifying and rehabilitating destitute children to 10 of its agencies.
 
• These agencies include the Child Welfare Committees (CWCs), District Child Protection Units (DCPUs), and various NGOs working for child welfare.
 
• The initiative aims to provide a safe environment and necessary resources for the overall development and well-being of destitute children in Delhi.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Women and Child Development (WCD) Department**

 
 
• The Women and Child Development (WCD) department is responsible for the development and protection of women and children in the state.
 
• It implements various schemes and programs aimed at improving the health, education, and social status of women and children.
 
• The department works closely with other governmental and non-governmental organizations to ensure effective implementation of its policies.
 
 
 
• **Child Welfare Committees (CWCs)**
 
 
• Child Welfare Committees (CWCs) are statutory bodies constituted under the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015.
 
• They are responsible for ensuring the care, protection, treatment, and rehabilitation of children in need of care and protection.
 
• CWCs have the authority to make decisions regarding the placement and welfare of such children.
 
 
 
• **District Child Protection Units (DCPUs)**
 
 
• District Child Protection Units (DCPUs) are established at the district level to implement child protection policies and programs.
 
• DCPUs coordinate with various stakeholders, including CWCs, NGOs, and law enforcement agencies, to ensure the safety and well-being of children.
 
• They also conduct awareness programs and provide support services to children and their families.
 
 
 
• **Non-Governmental Organizations (NGOs)**
 
 
• NGOs play a crucial role in the implementation of child welfare programs by providing on-ground support and resources.
 
• They work in collaboration with government agencies to identify, rescue, and rehabilitate destitute children.
 
• NGOs also provide educational, health, and vocational training services to help children lead a better life.
